Isolating Environmental Disturbances in BlueROV2 IMU Acceleration

A(t) = Φ(u(t)) + Δ(t): fitting the thruster response on calm-water data and tracking the residual current disturbance with a harmonic Kalman filter, then checking whether Φ stays consistent between calm and turbulent pool conditions.

Data. creo_pool "grab rod" task, BlueROV2, 50 Hz IMU/thruster logs, all 4 rod colors pooled per condition. CALM 99,805 frames · 405 episodes · 1996s    UNDER CURRENTS 124,307 frames · 415 episodes · 2486s

Executive summary

The headline result: the disturbance-correction step recovers a thruster model that matches the calm-water fit, where a naive fit does not. Fitting Φ directly on the under-currents data without removing the disturbance first gives a thruster gain matrix whose relative Frobenius distance from the calm-water Φ is 2.46 (and is even anti-correlated with it on the x-axis, cosine = -0.33). One round of alternating disturbance-estimation / Φ-refitting brings that down to a relative distance of 0.08, with per-axis cosine similarity of 0.999, 0.997, 0.999 — i.e. once the current's contribution is subtracted out, the recovered thruster-to-acceleration mapping is essentially the same physical constant in both pools, as Assumption 4 predicts.

Three supporting results: (1) the residual left after the calm-fit Φ is much louder under currents than in calm water at every frequency in the 10-3–10 Hz band, and grows a distinctive low-frequency (<0.1 Hz) component over the session that calm water never develops; (2) adding the disturbance estimate on top of Φ cuts held-out reconstruction RMSE substantially in both conditions; (3) gravity/orientation coupling is not optional — dropping it collapses held-out R² on the x-axis from 0.85 to 0.02.

Method

Per Assumption 2 (decoupled axes), each of acc_x, acc_y, acc_z is modeled independently as

A(t) ≈ G·[sin(pitch), sin(roll)cos(pitch), cos(roll)cos(pitch), 1] + Φ·u(t),   u(t) = thr1..6_pwm(t) − 1500

fit by ordinary least squares. The orientation terms span the possible gravity-projection directions so the fit finds the right IMU sign convention itself rather than it being assumed. Φ is estimated once on the calm set (80/20 episode-level train/test split) since Assumption 1's premise is that calm-water Δ(t) is small. The residual r(t) = A(t) − G·orient(t) − Φ·u(t) is then treated as the noisy measurement of Δ(t) in both conditions.

Δ(t) is modeled per Assumption 5–6 as a bank of K=41 real sinusoids log-spaced over 0.001–10.0 Hz. The Kalman state is the [a_k, b_k] coefficient pair per frequency, evolving as a random walk (process noise q=1e-05, selected by the ablation below) so the model can track Assumption 3's time-variance. Because the measurement model h(x,t) = H_t·x is linear in the state, a closed-form Kalman filter is mathematically exact here and is used for the full ~224,112-frame run; a generic from-scratch sigma-point UKF was also implemented (as method.md requests) and verified to reproduce the closed-form filter to within 1.1e-09 — see the equivalence check below.

Episodes have no shared absolute clock (each resets to t=0), so a synthetic per-condition clock (cumulative frame index × 20ms) is used to pool them for the filter and PSD analysis — see Limitations.

Does Φ survive the current? (core result)

FitFrobenius dist. (rel. to calm)cos(x)cos(y)cos(z)
Naive Φ on under-currents (no correction) 2.462-0.3270.5050.992
Disturbance-corrected Φ (1 alternation round) 0.0830.9990.9970.999
2nd alternation round 0.163 0.997 0.989 0.996

A 2nd alternation round doesn't improve on the 1st here — most of the correction is captured in one pass; further rounds mostly reshuffle noise between Φ and Δ̂. The y-axis (least-thrust-authority axis, smallest R² in the calm fit) is where the naive fit is corrupted the most and where correction has the most work to do.

Disturbance spectral content: calm vs. under currents

The residual left after removing Φ and gravity is louder under currents than in calm water across the entire 10-3–10 Hz band, not just at low frequency — consistent with turbulence adding broadband forcing on top of any slow current component.

The tracked disturbance amplitude |C_k(t)| (x-axis, K=41 bins) stays uniformly faint in calm water for the whole ~1996s session. Under currents, strong energy builds up specifically below ∼0.1 Hz and grows over the session — the signature of a slowly-varying current rather than a fixed-frequency vibration.

Reconstruction quality

Ablations

Frequency-bank size (K)

K=41 sits at the accuracy sweet spot on this data — more bins add compute without further reducing one-step prediction error.

Process noise (Q)

Too small a q makes the filter a static harmonic regression that can't track a time-varying current (Assumption 3); too large makes it chase measurement noise. q=1e-05 is the minimum on this sweep and is used as the baseline throughout.

Gravity/orientation term

Without the orientation regressors, thrusters alone explain almost none of the held-out variance (R²≈0.02–0.09) — the model would otherwise misattribute a large, non-oscillatory gravity-tilt bias to either Φ or Δ.

UKF implementation check

Since h(x,t) is linear, the unscented transform is exact: the from-scratch UKF and the closed-form KF agree to 1.1e-09 on 800 real residual samples — a sanity check on the UKF implementation, run at small scale since it is ~5× slower per step than the closed-form filter it's mathematically equivalent to here.

Limitations

  • No absolute clock across episodes. Each episode's timestamp resets to 0, so the pooled clock used here is synthetic (cumulative frame count × 20ms), not real elapsed time between episodes. True sub-∼0.05‑0.1 Hz content (below 1/episode-length) is not physically resolvable from real elapsed time even though the filter sweeps down to 10-3 Hz as specified — treat the lowest-frequency bins as informative about within-session drift rather than a calibrated absolute period.
  • Small-angle regime only. Roll/pitch stayed within ∼0.01–0.1 rad in this data; the orientation regressors are exact for gravity projection at any angle, but the thruster mixing matrix Φ is only linear-mixing-consistent near the trimmed attitude the vehicle was actually flown at.
  • u(t) = raw PWM, not thrust. BlueROV2 thrust vs. PWM is nominally close to linear near neutral but not exactly; Φ is therefore a local linear approximation valid over the PWM range actually commanded in these episodes (∼±100 μs of neutral).
  • Rod color is pooled and not treated as a covariate; a per-color breakdown was not run.

Conclusion

The proposed decomposition holds up on this data: a thruster model fit purely on calm water, applied unchanged to under-currents data, isolates a residual that (a) is spectrally distinct from calm-water noise, concentrated below 0.1 Hz and growing over the session, and (b) once tracked and subtracted, lets the under-currents data recover essentially the same thruster gain matrix as the calm fit (cosine similarity >0.98 on every axis after one correction round, vs. as low as -0.33 uncorrected). The harmonic Kalman filter is doing real work here — held-out reconstruction RMSE drops by roughly a third to a half in both conditions when its disturbance estimate is added to Φ alone.

Pipeline: src/load_data.py, src/model_phi.py, src/kalman.py, src/pipeline.py, src/plotting.py, src/report.py. Run end-to-end with python run.py (total runtime ≈24s on this dataset). Numeric results in outputs/results.json.
